name: Tempester n°19: an abandoned SysEx reception closes the Receiving screen
explanation: The reception screen (state handler [routine], child of [routine]) is opened by [routine](1, cmd) and consumes encoder, slider and button events and all non-SysEx MIDI events until a state-6 event or panel button 0x21. Three abandon paths reset the SysEx state without a state-6 event: (A) EOX while the substate is 0 (truncated 60 sound, 5C before its beat number, 61/62/70 stream before the last chunk), [routine] [address]; (B) a DIN status byte other than EOX during a DIN SysEx (cable = DIN), [routine] [address]; (C) a USB F0 while a USB reception is in progress, [routine] [address]. The screen then stays on "**** Receiving ... ****" and the machine looks frozen. Part 1: each path, when a reception was in progress (command != 0 and (byte counter != 0 or substate != 0)), resets first then publishes [routine](6, 0, 0, 0x25), the same (6, command 0) event the original error ends of [routine] (cases 61/62/70) publish after [routine]. Path B calls [routine] itself before publishing; the original call at [address] then resets an idle state, as for every DIN status byte. A finished reception is never in progress, so normal ends publish nothing more. Part 2: [routine] answered an end event for another command (command 0, or a different one) with return 3 (super), which leaves the state, and the stale text, unchanged; it now returns 2, a transition to [routine] (stored just after, unchanged), whose initial transition enters the boot screen [routine] (entry redraws it). Matched end events (normal results) and the 5E/5C project chain are untouched. Code: 0x9d07b900-0x9d07b9cf.

edits.why: jal 0x9d07b95c ; path A, [routine] substate 0: was "jal [address]" ([routine]); delay slot "li s0,0x25" kept (s0 preserved by the hook)
jal 0x9d07b95c ; path C, [routine] CIN 4 with F0: was "jal [address]" ([routine])

jal 0x9d07b900 ; path B, [routine] status byte 0x80-0xF7: was "beq v1,t3,[address]" (EOX test, t3 = 0xF7 set at [address]); the hook does the EOX test itself; delay slot (nop) kept; returns to [address]
li a0,0x2 ; [routine], end event (state 6) for another command: was "li a0,0x3" (super: the screen stayed); now a transition to [routine] (stored just after), which enters the boot screen
bne v1,t3,0x9d07b910 ; v1 = status byte, t3 = 0xF7, ra = [address]
j [address] ; EOX: the original branch target (end of SysEx, then rejoins [address]); ra is not used there
bne t0,t1,0x9d07b954 ; not DIN: a DIN status byte does not touch the SysEx in progress (n°6), nothing is abandoned
jal [address] ; DIN SysEx in progress: [routine](0) now (closes the file, resets); the one at [address] then resets an idle state, as for any DIN status byte
or s0,v0,zero ; delay slot: s0 = reception was in progress
lhu t1,-0x7f8c(gp) ; byte counter [address]: bytes still expected before the next step
lbu t2,-0x7f8a(gp) ; substate [address]: the EOX is still expected
sltu v0,zero,t1 ; v0 = 1 if either is non-zero
or a1,zero,zero ; command 0, as the original error ends
j [address] ; [routine](6, 0, 0, 0x25), returns to the caller; 0x25 = code of [routine] when the file never started
